requirements.label: physics
requirements.title: Physics Sequence Options

rule.manualCheck: At least one semester of the physics lecture/lab sequence must be passed with a letter grade of C or higher. The page lists no laboratory courses with the PHY 141/PHY 142 option; confirm with the department whether PHY 133/134 are also needed.

rules.manualCheck: With a Classical Physics option, a math course at the level of Calculus B (AMS 161, MAT 126, MAT 132, MAT 142, MAT 171) or higher is also required for the major. MAT 171 counts at that level but is already used by the calculus requirement, so confirm it yourself if that is your route.

With a Classical Physics option, a math course at the level of Calculus B (AMS 161, MAT 126, MAT 132, MAT 142, MAT 171) or higher is also required for the major. MAT 171 counts at that level but is already used by the calculus requirement, so confirm it yourself if that is your route.

With a Classical Physics option, a math course at the level of Calculus B (AMS 161, MAT 126, MAT 132, MAT 142, MAT 171) or higher is also required for the major. MAT 171 counts at that level but is already used by the calculus requirement, so confirm it yourself if that is your route.

requirements.label: advanced
requirements.title: Advanced Courses in Biology
requirements.sourceText: At least one of the following 3 credit upper division BIO courses: BIO 320 - General Genetics; BIO 321 - Ecological Genetics; BIO 354 - Evolution; EBH 302 - Human Genetics Two additional upper division BIO courses. Research, readings, teaching practica and internship courses cannot be used to satisfy upper-division BIO course requirements. Students cannot take both BIO 320 and BIO 321 for biology major credit. Only one of these courses may be taken for biology major credit.

requirements.label: upper-division-writing
requirements.title: Upper-Division Writing Requirement

rule.manualCheck: BIO 459 must be co-registered with an approved advanced course (BIO 312, 320, 321, 327, 335, 336, 344, 352, 353, 354, 364, 365, 366, 367, 385, 386 or EBH 302), and a lab report or term paper from that course must be submitted.

requirements.sourceText: In order to satisfy the Upper-Division Writing requirement for the major in Biology, students must co-register for the 0-credit BIO 459 course with an approved advanced course as listed below. Courses that routinely offer assignments that can satisfy the BIO 459 WRTD learning outcomes: BIO 312, BIO 320, BIO 321, BIO 327, BIO 335, BIO 336, BIO 344, BIO 352, BIO 353, BIO 354, BIO 364, BIO 365, BIO 366, BIO 367, BIO 385, BIO 386, EBH 302

policies.sourceText: All foundational courses in related fields must be taken for a letter grade; courses taken under the Pass/No Credit option will not count towards completion of the major, with the exception of the Spring 2020 semester. All core and advanced courses in biology must be taken for a letter grade and passed with a grade of C or higher.
All core and advanced courses in biology must be taken for a letter grade and passed with a grade of C or higher. The organic chemistry lab must be passed with a C or higher.
A letter grade of D or higher is accepted towards the statistics requirement for the following courses: AMS 110, AMS 310, BIO 211, or EBH 230.

Upper-division or upper-division equivalent courses taken elsewhere and transferred to Stony Brook can satisfy the requirement for BIO 320, BIO 321, BIO 354 or EBH 302 for the Biology BA; however, students must still take three advanced courses (300-level BIO courses) here at Stony Brook.

substitutions.condition: Students who transfer in AMS 102 from another institution with a grade of A or higher
substitutions.sourceText: Note: Students who transfer in AMS 102 from another institution with a grade of 'A' or higher will receive credit for the statistics course.

fulfillment.sourceText: Registration: The Upper Division Writing Requirement for the Biology major is consistent with the University Graduation Requirements for General Education, and successful completion will satisfy the Stony Brook Curriculum (SBC) learning outcomes for "Write Effectively within One's Discipline" (WRTD).

notes.text: Schedule advising appointments online through Navigate. Advisors: Rachel Pilero, Kayla McFadden, Allison Young. Office: Biology Learning Laboratories, Undergraduate Biology Office Suite, Rooms 104-112; phone (631) 632-8530.

The BA is for students who also pursue a non-overlapping minor; the BS (separate program) includes a specialization in place of that minor. Students in the Biology BA or BS may not declare a double major among Biology, Biochemistry, Pharmacology, Marine Sciences and Marine Vertebrate Biology. A double major in Biology and Human Evolutionary Biology requires a specific course combination set out in the EBH major requirements.
Courses taken under the Pass/No Credit option will not count towards completion of the major, except for the Spring 2020 semester.

Honors in Biology or in Biology and Society (not evaluated): cumulative GPA of 3.50 or higher in all courses required for the major; an acceptable thesis from at least two semesters of approved research or internship courses (BIO 484, 486, 487, 488, 489, MAR 487, MAR 488, ATM 487, BME 499); an Honors Application submitted to the Undergraduate Biology office by the second week of the last semester; and faculty endorsement and two readers.
Secondary teacher education: see the Education and Teacher Certification entry in the alphabetical listings of Approved Majors, Minors, and Programs.
Most students majoring in biology prepare for professional study in the biological or health sciences. Some prepare for secondary school teaching, and others for technical positions in industry.

The BA major requires at least 55 credits, plus the required minor (18-24 credits). Research, readings, teaching practica and internship courses cannot be used for the advanced biology courses. At least one semester of each two-semester sequence in general chemistry lecture, organic chemistry lecture and physics must be passed with a C or higher (flagged for confirmation on those requirements).

Complete a minor (18-24 credits) within the College of Arts and Sciences or the School of Communication and Journalism, with no more than a 3-credit overlap with the BA major requirements. Approved minors are listed on Undergraduate Biology's website.
